paper_metadata.title: Construction of a knowledge graph for framework material enabled by large language models and its application
paper_metadata.abstract: The study uses large language models to build KG-FM, a framework-material knowledge graph spanning synthesis, properties, applications, and related information for MOFs, COFs, and HOFs. It analyzes more than 100,000 articles, reports 2.53 million nodes and 4.01 million relationships, and evaluates KG-augmented question answering; Qwen2-KG is reported to achieve 91.67% accuracy with source information.

problem_addressed: Framework-material research is dispersed across a very large, fragmented literature, while no comprehensive FM knowledge graph had been constructed. Manual conversion of unstructured literature into connected domain knowledge is labor-intensive; the study aims to automate construction of a KG covering MOFs, COFs, and HOFs and use it for retrieval, mining, and more accurate, source-grounded LLM question answering.

methodology.primary_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
methodology.description: The paper presents KG-FM, a high-throughput Text-to-KG pipeline and a KG-augmented QA application. Execution order: (1) retrieve Web of Science records on MOF, COF, and HOF before 8 May 2024 and export abstracts plus bibliographic metadata as TXT; (2) prompt Qwen2-72B-Instruct to transform each abstract into structured JSON nodes and logical relations, with prompts defining tasks and output format; (3) manually inspect 100 LLM outputs; (4) convert JSON to Cypher and import it, along with title/DOI metadata and manually defined publication relations, into Neo4j 5.12.0; (5) query the graph directly or use a three-step RAG-style application that generates Cypher from a question, executes it over Neo4j, and formulates an answer from retrieved KG data. The study's central contributions are the large KG-FM resource, prompt-based abstract-to-JSON extraction, Neo4j graph construction, and evaluation/demonstration of KG-supported LLM retrieval and chain-of-thought material-screening reasoning.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The paper uses a prompt-specified JSON output structure with logical relations, then maps the resulting nodes and relationships to Neo4j. It additionally defines publication/provenance relations manually, including “Derived from”, “Published in (Journal)”, and “Published at (Date)”. It does not report use of a formal external ontology or a formal ontology-learning procedure.

input_output.input_type: Web of Science bibliographic records: unstructured academic-paper abstracts for MOF, COF, and HOF literature, supplemented with structured publication metadata including DOI, authors, publication date, journal, and title.
input_output.input_granularity: One scientific-paper abstract at a time for LLM extraction; more than 100,000 retrieved journal articles in the final corpus.
input_output.output_representation: Prompt-generated structured JSON containing extracted nodes and relationships; Cypher queries; and a Neo4j property-graph knowledge graph (KG-FM) with material, property, structure, synthesis, application, report, and publication/provenance information.

models_and_tools: Qwen2-72B-Instruct for abstract extraction and Qwen2-KG QA
datasets: Web of Science corpus of MOF, COF, and HOF articles published before 8 May 2024; more than 100,000 articles
Manual sample of 100 LLM-extracted abstract results
150-question framework-material QA test set with reference answers

metrics: Abstract extraction: true-positive rate for accurate and comprehensive information extraction; false-negative rate; F1 score
QA: manually judged answer accuracy/correctness; standard error
evaluation.setting: Extraction quality was assessed by manual review of 100 LLM outputs, treating an extraction as a true positive only when relations were accurate and comprehensive. QA was evaluated on 150 framework-material questions and reference answers available in the project repository; two domain experts manually judged answers correct only when they supplied accurate information without misleading content. The paper also gives qualitative retrieval, mining, and CoT screening demonstrations (BUT-55 and industrial SO2 adsorbent design).

value: KG-FM built from more than 100,000 articles contains more than 2.53 million nodes and 4.01 million relationships. Table 2 reports MOF/COF/HOF literature counts of 68,400/21,776/15,203; nodes of 1,351,477/553,888/628,341; and relationships of 2,439,563/809,375/757,736.
On manual review of 100 abstract extractions, the authors report 98% true-positive rate, 2% false-negative rate, and F1=0.9898 for accurate and comprehensive information extraction.

On the 150-question QA set, Table 3 reports Qwen2-KG 91.67% accuracy (standard error 0.47%); GLM4-KG 80.67% (0.94%); Llama3-KG 88.33% (1.41%); versus Qwen2 14.33%, GLM4 5.67%, Llama3 8.00%, GPT4 33.33%, and Copilot 31.33%. The text separately reports Qwen2-KG as 91.67 ± 0.94%, which conflicts with the table's stated standard error.

Qualitatively, the KG-enabled Qwen2 retrieves and answers BUT-55 structure/property questions through Cypher when the material name is not explicitly in the source abstract, and the KG context enables a more reasonable SO2 adsorbent recommendation in the reported CoT demonstration.

value: Author-supported: provides a documented, high-throughput pipeline from abstracts to a large domain-specific graph, retaining publication metadata and source links.
Experimental: manual extraction assessment reports high relation-extraction quality (98% TP; F1 0.9898) on the inspected 100-output sample.
Experimental: KG augmentation substantially improves reported QA accuracy for the tested Qwen2, GLM4, and Llama3 models on the same 150-question test set.
Review-level inference: the separate JSON, Cypher, and Neo4j stages make intermediate structured outputs inspectable and enable direct graph queries in addition to natural-language QA.

value: Review-level inference: extraction is limited to abstracts, so experimental detail, methods, caveats, and information present only in full text are systematically outside the reported extraction input.

Review-level inference: the extraction evaluation manually reviews only 100 outputs and reports no held-out, independently annotated corpus or inter-annotator agreement, limiting the precision of quality claims for a graph built from more than 100,000 papers.

Review-level inference: the QA evaluation is manual and limited to 150 in-domain questions; it does not report retrieval metrics, error categories, question sampling protocol, or a blind adjudication process.

Review-level inference: prompt definitions are referenced only through supplementary figures, and manual relationship definitions influence graph semantics, which may make replication and transfer to another domain dependent on unreported design choices.

value: The authors state that chain-of-thought techniques heavily rely on background knowledge and that, without sufficient background knowledge, even structured reasoning cannot produce good answers.

value: Author-proposed: introduce KG answers before CoT reasoning and further integrate KG with CoT to enhance scientific-discovery capability.
Review-level inference: extend extraction beyond abstracts and evaluate node/relation correctness against a larger, independently annotated benchmark with relation-level error analysis.
Review-level inference: add automated provenance checks, schema/constraint validation, and systematic evaluation of Cypher generation and retrieval separately from answer generation.

evidence.excerpt: In the future, integrating KG with CoT’s thinking process may further enhance its ability for scientific discovery.

value: Review-level inference: reliable extraction of complete, context-sensitive scientific claims remains unresolved when the system processes abstracts rather than full papers.

Review-level inference: scalability of manual graph-quality assurance and maintenance as new framework-material literature appears is unresolved; the paper does not report a graph-updating or ongoing validation process.

Review-level inference: whether the QA gains generalize beyond the authors' 150-question FM test set, or remain robust to incorrect/ambiguous graph content and generated Cypher queries, is unresolved.
Review-level inference: formal ontology alignment, entity normalization across synonyms/material aliases, and reproducible semantic governance of the large graph are not evaluated in the paper.
